extracted.intended_audience: USPTO stakeholders, patent and trademark practitioners, applicants, and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Performance, quality, timeliness, and operational criteria used by the USPTO to evaluate and improve patent examination, PTAB proceedings, and trademark examination and register integrity. Includes AI/IT, training, stakeholder engagement, and enforcement-related standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI search system capabilities and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: AI-based prototype search system that helps to identify relevant documents and provides suggestions for other areas to search; designed to learn from USPTO examiners via automatically captured feedback data; includes features to help examiners interpret results generated by the AI models to provide transparency into the system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: System should provide relevant-document identification, search-area suggestions, capture examiner feedback for ongoing improvements, and include interpretability indicators so examiners can understand model reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auto-classification tool functionality and explainability
rubrics_metrics.description: Auto-classification tool leveraging machine learning to classify patent documents using the Cooperative Patent Classification (CPC) system; can suggest CPC symbols, identify claimed subject matter for refinement, and includes indicators linking suggested CPC symbols to specific portions of the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tool should suggest CPC codes, identify claimed subject matter, provide explainability by linking suggestions to text segments, integrate feedback with existing classification processes, and support expansion to broader classification requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI training via examiner feedback integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhanced feedback mechanisms integrate with USPTO’s existing classification processes to support training the AI; system automatically captures feedback data from examiners to yield further enhancements over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational requirement that AI systems capture and use examiner feedback as training data to improve performance and ensure alignment with examiner judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtual onboarding and training (Patent Training Academy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Training Academy onboards and trains new employees in the virtual environment without requiring relocation; optimizes offerings focusing on interactivity and community connectivity to acclimate new examiners to USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training programs should support remote delivery, emphasize interactive and community-building elements, and enable nationwide examiner recruitment and onboarding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telework program flexibility and expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: Expanded and streamlined telework programs to allow the vast majority of employees to work remotely full-time, supporting a nationwide workforce without requiring relocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Telework policies should be flexible and streamlined to enable remote work while maintaining mission continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusive outreach and stakeholder engagement (CI2 / NCEAI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Council for Inclusive Innovation (formerly NCEAI) composed of leaders from government, industry, academia, nonprofits, venture capitalists, and independent inventors to increase participation in the innovation ecosystem demographically, geographically, and economically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outreach should prioritize inclusivity across demographics, geography, and economic backgrounds and host educational events (e.g., Innovation Chat webinars) to increase participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidated stakeholder support (OPSE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Office of Patents Stakeholder Experience (OPSE) consolidates stakeholder education, support, and customer experience to optimize resources and assist external stakeholders regardless of skill level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralize customer assistance functions to provide consistent help with filing and prosecution issues across multiple channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro Se Assistance Program accessibility and channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Pro Se Assistance Program helps independent inventors and small businesses via virtual one-on-one, telephone, email assistance, and virtual education programs; operates Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. ET.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accessible, multi-channel assistance for pro se applicants with set operating hours and virtual appointment options to reduce barriers and increase transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactive collaboration with applicants to reduce procedural obstacles
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent examiners in the Pro Se Art Unit work with applicants from filing through final disposition (abandoned, allowed, or on appeal) to identify, streamline, and ameliorate procedural obstacles for first-time filers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish proactive examiner-applicant collaboration workflows to identify common procedural issues and streamline processes for inexperienced filers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer partnership meetings for technology-specific issues
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO-hosted Customer Partnership Meetings (including virtual meetings) focused on specific technology areas (e.g., cybersecurity, business methods) to enhance relationships and improve prosecutorial issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hold stakeholder meetings targeted by technology area to gather feedback and address prosecution challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remote hearing access and public participation (PTAB)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conducted ex parte appeal hearings and AIA trial hearings remotely by telephone or video since the pandemic and granted public access to certain proceedings by telephone, a service not offered before the pandemic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide remote hearing modalities and mechanisms for public access to increase transparency and continuity of proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner training and feedback (LEAP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex parte appeal or AIA trial arguments involving practitioners participating in the Legal Experience and Advancement Program (LEAP) and mock argument training sessions including personalized feedback for each practitioner from actual judges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement practitioner training programs that include mock arguments and personalized judge feedback to improve practitioner competence and experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation and summary of public comments on procedural discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: Published a request for comments concerning the discretion to institute AIA trials and released a summary of more than 800 comments received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use formal public-comment processes and publish summaries to inform procedural policy changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of procedural rule changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Published final rules allocating the burden of persuasion on motions to amend in AIA trials and eliminating the presumption at institution favoring the petitioner as to testimonial evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicate substantive procedural rule changes clearly and implement them in practice; ensure stakeholders are aware of how burdens and evidentiary presumptions are allocated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on substantive standards and interim processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Published guidance on the indefiniteness standard applied in AIA post-grant proceedings and on implementation of a new, interim Director review process under Arthrex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issue guidance documents to clarify standards of review and new internal review processes to ensure consistent application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fast-track ex parte appeal pilot timeliness targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Granted 181 petitions for entry into the fast-track ex parte appeal pilot program within an average of 1.4 days of petition filing and issued 128 appeal decisions within an average of 2.2 months of petition grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pilot programs with explicit timeliness performance metrics (e.g., petition grant turnaround and decision issuance averages) to expedite particular appeal types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority pilot programs for critical technologies (e.g., COVID-19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Implemented a pilot program to expedite the review of decisions in ex parte appeals covering inventions related to COVID-19.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish targeted expedited review tracks for inventions of urgent public importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim Director review process to address Arthrex implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Implemented an interim Director review process allowing parties to request Director review of a final written decision or the Director to conduct review on their own accord to ensure APJs function as inferior officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a mechanism for Director review of PTAB decisions to address separation-of-powers and appointment issues and to preserve decision validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB statutory due-date compliance and pendency goals
rubrics_metrics.description: PTAB continued to meet all statutory due dates for AIA proceedings and reduced average pendency of ex parte appeals from ~30 months (2015) to 12.7 months (Q4 FY2021). The Board has a long-term pendency goal of 12 months in ex parte appeals in all technology areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track statutory due-date compliance and set explicit pendency targets (e.g., 12 months for ex parte appeals) and report progress annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB IT consolidation (P-TACTS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Converting from multisystem PTAB End-to-End IT system to a single integrated Patent Trial and Appeal Case Tracking System (P-TACTS) to provide improved unified interfaces, straightforward external filing UI, better analytics, dashboards, and comprehensive reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consolidate disparate IT systems into a unified platform to improve user experience, case management, analytics, and reporting; iterate based on internal and external feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of decision to institute (PTAB metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Target timeliness for decision to institute: 3.0 (months implied by Table 12 targets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor and report actual average time to institution decisions against a 3.0-month target; indicate whether target met.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA trial proceedings timeliness (PTAB metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Target timeliness for AIA trial proceedings: 12.0 months (as given in Table 13).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track average months for trial proceedings from institution to decision and compare to 12-month target.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pendency of decided appeals (PTAB metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average number of months from appeal number assignment date to decided appeals, with target goal (long-term) of 12 months; historical actuals reported (e.g., 12.7 months in FY2021).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure average appeal pendency and pursue strategies to meet the 12-month goal across technology areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark registration benefits (legal criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal registration provides notice to the public of registrant’s claim, legal presumption of ownership nationwide, and a presumption of the exclusive right to use the mark on or in connection with identified goods/services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage registrants to seek federal registration to obtain nationwide presumptions and enforcement advantages; communicate CBP recording benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark examination core practices and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Examining attorneys search electronic databases for confusingly similar marks, examine applications for compliance with statutory and procedural requirements, communicate findings to applicants, review responses, approve applications for publication, and examine statements of use and maintenance/renewal filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination should comprehensively address registrability, confusion likelihood, statutory compliance, and proper handling of post-approval maintenance matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: First action pendency target and measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: First action pendency measures time from USPTO receipt of a trademark application to when it is first pulled for examination; FY2021 first action pendency exceeded target, with target ranges historically set (examples: 2.5–4.5 months in FY2021).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set and monitor first action pendency target ranges (e.g., 2.5–4.5 months), measure monthly trends, and report deviations with remediation plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final disposal pendency target
rubrics_metrics.description: Final disposal measures time from filing to registration or abandonment; FY2021 average was 11.2 months against a 12-month target.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to meet final disposal target (12 months) through capacity adjustments and process improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational surge-response strategies for trademark filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Multi-faceted strategies include reorganizing workloads, hiring additional examining attorneys, increasing overtime, streamlining work processes (including exploring robotic process automation), and launching pilot programs with specialized contractors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt flexible capacity models and process automation to respond to unexpected filing volume surges while maintaining quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: First action compliance rate (quality metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: First action compliance rate is the number of first actions without substantive decision-making errors, substantive errors missed, or substandard refusals under section 2 divided by total first actions reviewed; FY2021 target 95.5%, actual 96.3%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use defined compliance criteria to audit first actions and maintain or improve above-target compliance rates via training and feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final action compliance rate (quality metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final compliance rate is total number of cases without substantive decision-making errors divided by total reviewed final actions and cases approved for publication; FY2021 target 97.0%, actual 98.7%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit final actions against substantive decision-making standards and maintain a high approval/denial accuracy rate through continuing education and review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptional office action rate and definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Exceptional office actions are cases with no decision-making errors, a sufficient search, and writing and evidence for every issue rated as 'excellent'; target (FY2021) 50.0%, actual 54.1%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure and target a high rate of exceptional office actions by focusing on search quality, thorough evidence development, and exemplary writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holistic quality criteria for office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality measurement considers application’s adherence to registrability standards and the comprehensive excellence of the office action itself, including research, writing, legal decision-making, and evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality assessments should be holistic—evaluating legal reasoning, search sufficiency, clarity of writing, and supporting evidence for each issue raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner training and continuing education standards
rubrics_metrics.description: New examining attorneys are trained in classroom then mentored; continuing training includes in-house legal training, case law updates, external CLE, and best practices for IT use and error minimization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain structured initial training plus ongoing legal and technical education, mentorship, and training on IT tools to sustain high-quality examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder engagement for quality verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage stakeholders via industry-specific training, roundtables, meetings, a customer call center, and email to verify trademark quality findings and update identifications of goods and services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate external stakeholder feedback mechanisms into quality assurance and policy updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficiency metric: cost per trademark office disposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Efficiency measured by dividing total trademark-related expenses (including multiyear IT investments, overhead, allocated expenses) by outputs or office disposals (abandoned and registered applications, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track cost-per-disposal over time to evaluate process efficiency and compare against targets and budgeted expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: IT modernization practices (DevSecOps and blue/green)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopted DevSecOps pipelines and parallel 'blue/green' environments for over 90% of the Trademarks Product Line to allow faster delivery of software into production and increased system availability with no downtime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement DevSecOps and blue/green deployment strategies to shorten time-to-production, reduce downtime risk, and improve system reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usability testing for user-facing tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Completed initial usability testing for a new log-in identity verification and attorney sponsorship tool for TEAS filers; collected participant feedback to finalize requirements to ensure positive customer experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct usability testing with representative users and incorporate feedback into final requirements to improve CX for filing systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of business intelligence and analytics to guide decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Expanded Trademarks business intelligence analysts (including AI/ML expertise) and released dashboard products providing granular insights into goods/services driving filings and suspicious/fraudulent filings; analytics efforts included proof-of-use reporting automation, misclassification identification, applicant profile and growth analysis, and digitally altered specimen analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in data analytics and AI to detect fraud patterns, improve classification accuracy, forecast filing trends, and inform operational decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protecting the integrity of the Trademark Register
rubrics_metrics.description: Initiatives include administrative sanctions for improper submissions (investigate violations of Trademark Rules of Practice and USPTO website terms of use, impose sanctions, refer for discipline or law enforcement), and other operational and statutory adjustments to address fake or digitally altered specimens and false information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish investigative and enforcement mechanisms (administrative sanctions, referrals to discipline or law enforcement) and fee-based or procedural remedies to deter and address fraudulent filings.
